key_insight: A deformation-dependent semisoft modulus enables a transversely isotropic model to capture stiffness anisotropy and finite-onset, broad semisoft plateaus in main-chain liquid crystal elastomers.
engineering_relevance: The model supports orientation-dependent predictions of large-strain elastic response for liquid crystal elastomer components.
method: Combine finite-strain, isothermal network elasticity with a deformation-dependent quadratic semisoft penalty.
Use a weak-fluctuation statistical closure to obtain exponential evolution from an initial to a residual semisoft modulus.
Derive perpendicular-tension relations and model coupled director rotation, shear and lateral contraction under oblique tension.
evidence_signal: Comparisons with orientation-dependent measurements using one common parameter set capture the principal stiffness contrast and broad perpendicular plateau.
watch_item: Discrepancies remain in oblique stresses and intermediate-angle initial moduli, limiting confidence outside the best-matched loading orientations.
paper_title: A transversely isotropic constitutive model for semisoft elasticity in main-chain liquid crystal elastomers
